header.title: Components
header.description: Every component of the library, with its variants, a playground, examples with their code and its props.

api.caption: Props of {{component}}
api.native: Attribute of the native element, passed on unchanged.

button.summary: Action with a visible text label.
button.description: Use it for actions inside the page: saving, confirming, opening a dialog. Mark the main action of a view with the `official` intent; to go to another page, use a `Link`.

actions.title: Actions of a form
actions.description: One `official` solid button for the main action; the others stay soft or ghost.

loading.title: Operation in progress
loading.description: `loading` keeps the label, the look and the focus while the action runs, and tells assistive technologies that the button is busy.

accessibility.name: The visible label is the accessible name; for a button with only an icon, use `IconButton`.
accessibility.type: It is a native button with `type="button"`; pass `type="submit"` in forms.
accessibility.loading: `loading` sets `aria-busy` and ignores activation without taking the focus away; `disabled` means the action is unavailable.

iconButton.summary: Action shown only as an icon, named by a required label.
iconButton.description: Use it where space is short and the icon is well known: a toolbar, the actions of a row, the controls of a player. The `label` says what the action does; when the icon alone is not obvious, use a `Button` with `startIcon`.

actions.title: Actions of a row
actions.description: Ghost icon buttons, each one named after the action and the item it acts on; `error` marks the destructive one.

playback.title: Player controls
playback.description: A large solid button for the main action, whose `label` follows the action it performs next.

accessibility.name: `label` is the accessible name (`aria-label`) and cannot be blank: name the action, e.g. `Remove Spike Spiegel`, not the icon.
accessibility.icon: The icon is hidden from assistive technologies; mark it `decorative`.
accessibility.target: Every size is a square of at least 32 px, above the WCAG 2.2 minimum target.

copyButton.summary: Copies a text to the clipboard and confirms it.
copyButton.description: Put it next to a value the reader will paste elsewhere: a code, a key, a link. `value` can be a function, called at the moment of the copy.

inline.title: Next to a value
inline.description: The icon alone, named by `label` after what it copies.

invite.title: With its name
invite.description: `showLabel` shows the name next to the icon, for a copy that is the main action of its area.

accessibility.name: Name it after what it copies, e.g. `Copy invite link`; the name never changes under the focus.
accessibility.announcement: The result (`Copied`, or `Could not copy`) is announced by a live region and shown by the icon and the intent, not by the color alone.
accessibility.clipboard: The Clipboard API needs a secure context (HTTPS or `localhost`); elsewhere the copy fails and says so.

chip.summary: Compact label for an attribute, a status or a filter.
chip.description: A chip with only a label is text; with `onClick` it is a button, with `selected` a toggle, and `onDelete` gives it a separate delete button.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: Soft chips, one intent per status, with the status written in the label.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: Selectable chips in a named group: each one is a toggle button.

accessibility.text: A chip without `onClick` is plain text, not a control.
accessibility.toggle: With `onClick` it is a native button; with `selected` it is a toggle with `aria-pressed`, and its check mark is a shape besides the color.
accessibility.remove: The delete button is separate, a tab stop of its own, named by `deleteLabel`, e.g. `Remove Status: open`.

avatar.summary: Picture or initials of a person or an entity.
avatar.description: Shows the image of `src`, or the initials of `name` when there is none or it fails to load. The `name` is also its accessible name, unless `decorative` hides it next to a name already written.

profile.title: Next to the name
profile.description: The name is written beside it, so the avatar is `decorative` and is not read twice.

crew.title: A crew
crew.description: Avatars alone in a list: each one is named by its `name`, and the initials come from its first and last words.

accessibility.name: Without `decorative`, the avatar is an image (`role='img'`) named by `name`; the initials are hidden.
accessibility.decorative: With `decorative` it is hidden from assistive technologies: use it when the name is next to it.
accessibility.image: With `src`, the image takes `name` as its `alt`, or an empty `alt` when decorative.

badge.summary: Count or dot attached to an element, e.g. unread messages.
badge.description: Wraps the element it marks. `content` takes a number or a short text, and numbers above `max` show as `99+`; `dot` shows a dot instead, and `invisible` hides it when there is nothing new.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: A count with a `label` read after the button; the second button already says the count, so its badge is `decorative`.

presence.title: Presence
presence.description: Dots on avatars tell who is online; `invisible` hides the dot of someone offline.

accessibility.label: The visual count is hidden from assistive technologies: `label` states what it means, as hidden text next to the element.
accessibility.decorative: Mark it `decorative` when the element already says it, e.g. an `IconButton` labelled `Alerts, 120 unread`.
accessibility.dot: A dot has no text, so its `label` is the only way to tell what it means.

card.summary: Raised surface grouping related content, with an optional header.
card.description: `CardHeader` gives a title and its subtitle, with room for an avatar before and controls after; `CardContent` holds the rest. `variant='elevated'` adds a shadow for a card over other content.

parts.cardHeader: The title of the card, a heading of `headingLevel`, with its `subtitle`, `avatar` and `action`.
parts.cardContent: The body of the card, in secondary text.

profile.title: A profile
profile.description: A `section` named by its title, with an avatar, an actions button and chips in the content.

articles.title: Entries of a log
articles.description: A list of `article` cards in a `Grid`, each one with its heading one level below the section.

accessibility.region: With `as='section'` or `as='article'`, the card is a region named by the title of its `CardHeader`, or by `aria-label` without one.
accessibility.heading: Pick `headingLevel` from the outline of the page, not from the size: the title looks the same at any level.
accessibility.actions: Links and buttons go in `action` or in the content, never around the whole card.

carousel.summary: Slides shown one at a time, with buttons to move between them.
carousel.description: Each child is a slide. The previous and next buttons and one button per position move between them; `loop` goes from the last to the first. It never moves by itself.

reports.title: Reports
reports.description: Cards as slides, with `loop` so the next button of the last slide goes back to the first.

controlled.title: Controlled
controlled.description: `index` and `onIndexChange` keep the slide in the state of the parent, which shows it and can move it.

accessibility.region: A region named by `label`, announced as a carousel; each slide is a group named by its position, e.g. `2 of 3`.
accessibility.keyboard: The arrow keys move between slides and Home and End go to the ends; the position buttons are a single tab stop.
accessibility.hidden: The hidden slides are `inert`: their content is neither focused nor read.
accessibility.motion: There is no autoplay, and the transition is instant with reduced motion.

divider.summary: Thin line separating groups of content.
divider.description: Horizontal by default, between blocks; `orientation='vertical'` separates the items of a row and stretches to its height.

toolbar.title: Groups of buttons
toolbar.description: A vertical divider between the editing buttons and the others of a row.

sections.title: Sections
sections.description: A separator between the header and the details, and a `decorative` line before a note.

accessibility.separator: It is announced as a separator, vertical ones with `aria-orientation`.
accessibility.decorative: With `decorative` it is hidden from assistive technologies: use it when headings or lists already group the content.
accessibility.contrast: The line is lighter than 3:1, so the grouping never depends on it alone: keep the spacing or the headings.

list.summary: A list of records, one per row, with content before and after each one.
list.description: Each `ListItem` has a title, an optional supporting line, and `leading` and `trailing` content such as an `Avatar`, a value or a `Chip`. `ordered` renders an ordered list.

parts.listItem: A row: its `title` and `description`, between `leading` and `trailing`.

crew.title: Crew
crew.description: Decorative avatars before each name, since the title already says it, and a status chip after.

ranking.title: Ranking
ranking.description: An `ordered` list, whose position is announced; the title writes it too, since the list has no markers.

accessibility.count: A native list, `ul` or `ol`: assistive technologies announce the number of items and the position of each one.
accessibility.controls: Links and buttons go in `title` or `trailing`, never around the whole item.
accessibility.table: For records compared column by column, use a `Table`.

statCard.summary: Key figure of a dashboard: what is measured, its value and how it changed.
statCard.description: `change` gives the variation and its trend, whose color follows the sentiment: a rising cost is `negative`. `description` adds the context, and `loading` shows a placeholder.

indicators.title: Indicators
indicators.description: Three cards in a `Grid`: a rising revenue, a rising cost with `sentiment: 'negative'`, and no change.

loading.title: Loading
loading.description: `loading` replaces the value and the change with a placeholder, and announces that it loads.

accessibility.trend: The trend is told by an arrow and by hidden text, e.g. `Up 12%`, and the sentiment by color: neither rests on color alone.
accessibility.loading: While it loads, the card is `aria-busy` and announces `labels.loading` in place of the value.

container.summary: Centers the content of a page or a section and limits its width.
container.description: Wrap the content of a page in it: `size` limits the line length (`small` for reading and forms, `large` for dashboards) and the side gutters grow with the viewport.

article.title: A text to read
article.description: A `small` container keeps the lines short enough to read, as an `article`.

accessibility.landmark: `as` gives it the element of its role: `main` once per page for its main content, `article` or `section` for a region; name a `section` with `aria-label`.

stack.summary: Lays its children out in a column or a row, with a gap from the spacing scale.
stack.description: The layout of most groups: fields of a form, buttons of a toolbar, items of a list. `direction` and `gap` take one value or one per breakpoint, e.g. `{ compact: 'column', medium: 'row' }`.

header.title: Header of a section
header.description: A column on a phone and a row from `medium` up, with the title and the actions at the ends.

list.title: A list
list.description: `as='ul'` with `li` children keeps the list semantics without bullets or indentation.

accessibility.order: Keep the visual order the order of the code: the reading and focus order follow the code, not the layout.
accessibility.list: With `as='ul'` or `as='ol'`, each child must be an `li`, and the list is announced with its number of items.

grid.summary: Two-dimensional layout: equal columns per breakpoint, or as many columns as fit.
grid.description: `columns` sets the number of equal columns, per breakpoint if needed; `minColumnWidth` instead fits as many columns of that width as the space allows, without media queries.

parts.gridItem: A cell that spans several columns, or the whole row with `span='full'`.

dashboard.title: Panels of a dashboard
dashboard.description: One column on a phone, two on a tablet and four on a laptop, where the first panel spans two.

gallery.title: A gallery
gallery.description: `minColumnWidth` fits the cards to the width; as a list, each `GridItem` is an `li`.

accessibility.order: The reading and focus order follow the code, not the cells: place the items in the order they are read.
accessibility.list: A collection is a list: `as='ul'` with `GridItem as='li'`.
